name: CppServer
listed_description: Ultra fast and low latency asynchronous socket server & client C++ library with support TCP, SSL, UDP, HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket protocols and 10K connections problem solution.
reason: README Performance section has only self-measurements (Windows 8, i7-4790K: e.g. TCP echo round-trip 5625528 msg/s at 177 ns, HTTP trace server 307154 msg/s) with no named baseline library. Issue #2 'performances' asks for a comparison with uWebSockets but holds no numbers; no benchmark repo or shootout including it was reachable.

name: CSerialPort
reason: No benchmark anywhere in README or docs; the README TODO list still shows '6.Performance test report (Throughput && delay && packet dropout rates)' unchecked. 'Lightweight' is a design claim with no numbers or baseline.

name: DPDK
listed_description: Data Plane Development Kit, libraries and drivers for fast packet processing.
reason: Repo README and docs carry no comparison against libpcap or the Linux kernel stack (repo page shows no benchmark; libpcap PR #790 has none). Third-party comparisons exist (Gallenmueller et al. ANCS 2015, dpdk.org PacketCapture.pdf, a mathnet.ru capture-tools paper, Hemminger DPDK-Performance slides) but www.net.in.tum.de, www.dpdk.org, mathnet.ru, inbox.dpdk.org, osti.gov and diva-portal were EGRESS_BLOCKED, and the GitHub repos found (dpdkcap, DPDK2disk, DPDK-Replay, afxdp_perfeval, packetcapture) hold no DPDK-versus-baseline numbers. Worth retrying from an environment that reaches those hosts; the ANCS paper compares DPDK with netmap and PF_RING ZC, so the strongest baseline may be the Linux kernel stack rather than libpcap.

name: Dyad.c
reason: README states only a design aim ('lightweight, portable and easy to use'); no benchmark, doc/api.md or repo page mentions numbers or a baseline. Repo archived, last commit 2021-05-27, MIT, about 1.5k stars.
